prompt: Create a NEW character/style development sheet for a graphic ink MANHUA comic, portrait 2:3. Clean WHITE paper. This is NOT realistic watercolor illustration: visibly economical dip-pen and broad black brush shapes, thick and thin contour lines, flat muted OCHRE fills on golden fur, flat DARK UMBER fills on dark fur, pale tan faces, no gradients, no glossy highlights, no paper grain. Do NOT render individual hairs: at most a handful of large silhouette tufts, interior fur treated as flat shape; leave white highlights and strong deliberate BLACK shadows. Think graphic comic drawing, with expressive acting, believable monkey hands and feet, sturdy muscular shapes, no plush-toy round anatomy, no big shiny cute eyes. Uncluttered white negative space, no scenery, no labels or text. Two rows for two ANIMAL monkeys, no human garments, no genitals. First row: golden-brown stone monkey, lean adolescent-sized body, long tail, swept spiky golden hair in 5-7 bold tufts, narrow tan projecting muzzle, modest amber eyes. Show standing front three-quarter, profile, crouching startled pose, and two LARGE faces: alert open eyebrow with gaze to LEFT, then a dry deadpan half-lidded expression and relaxed mouth (NOT angry). Second row: dark-brown male monkey, slightly longer forearms, longer darker muzzle, less spiky dark hair, distinct MISSING V NOTCH in LEFT ear upper rim (viewer RIGHT in frontal view), long tail; standing front three-quarter, side on a branch implied by single black line, crouching ready-to-run, and two LARGE faces: curious skeptical one raised brow with lips slightly parted, then alarmed mouth open. All poses in same coherent proportions and matte restrained colored ink style. No textures made from endless tiny stripes, no detailed leaf/rock motifs, no watercolor blooming over entire page. No comic page layout, no captions. This sheet tests NEW line and color treatment while preserving original character identity markers.
